title: Assignment 09 · Battle of the forms and later-delivered terms
summary: Battle of the forms and later-delivered terms. Assigned readings and principal cases for this class.
notes:
Bayway Refining Co. v. Oxygenated Marketing & Trading A.G.: The buyer failed to establish that an added, customary tax-allocation clause materially altered this merchant contract, so the clause became part of it under § 2-207(2).

Northrop Corp. v. Litronic Industries: The court predicted that Illinois would apply the knockout approach to conflicting warranty terms, although it preferred another interpretation of § 2-207.

Hill v. Gateway 2000, Inc.: The Seventh Circuit treated retention beyond the stated return period as acceptance of the seller’s package terms, including arbitration, under its deferred-formation approach.

Klocek v. Gateway, Inc.: Gateway failed to show assent to its package arbitration terms. The court treated the consumer’s order as the offer and the later terms as proposals requiring agreement.

Additional assigned materials: UCC § 2-207; Restatement of Consumer Contracts § 2(b), (c).
